lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: # Design It Twice

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: When the user wants to explore alternative interfaces for a chosen deepening candidate, use this parallel sub-agent pattern. Based on "Design It Twice" (Ousterhout) — your first idea is unlikely to be the best.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Uses the vocabulary in [SKILL.md](SKILL.md) — **module**, **interface**, **seam**, **adapter**, **leverage**.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ## Process

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ### 1. Frame the problem space

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Before spawning sub-agents, write a user-facing explanation of the problem space for the chosen candidate:

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - The constraints any new interface would need to satisfy

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - The dependencies it would rely on, and which category they fall into (see [DEEPENING.md](DEEPENING.md))

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - A rough illustrative code sketch to ground the constraints — not a proposal, just a way to make the constraints concrete

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Show this to the user, then immediately proceed to Step 2. The user reads and thinks while the sub-agents work in parallel.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ### 2. Spawn sub-agents

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Spawn 3+ sub-agents in parallel using the Agent tool. Each must produce a **radically different** interface for the deepened module.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Prompt each sub-agent with a separate technical brief (file paths, coupling details, dependency category from [DEEPENING.md](DEEPENING.md), what sits behind the seam). The brief is independent of the user-facing problem-space explanation in Step 1. Give each agent a different design constraint:

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - Agent 1: "Minimize the interface — aim for 1–3 entry points max. Maximise leverage per entry point."

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - Agent 2: "Maximise flexibility — support many use cases and extension."

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - Agent 3: "Optimise for the most common caller — make the default case trivial."

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - Agent 4 (if applicable): "Design around ports & adapters for cross-seam dependencies."

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Include both [SKILL.md](SKILL.md) vocabulary and CONTEXT.md vocabulary in the brief so each sub-agent names things consistently with the architecture language and the project's domain language.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Each sub-agent outputs:

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: 1. Interface (types, methods, params — plus invariants, ordering, error modes)

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: 2. Usage example showing how callers use it

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: 3. What the implementation hides behind the seam

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: 4. Dependency strategy and adapters (see [DEEPENING.md](DEEPENING.md))

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: 5. Trade-offs — where leverage is high, where it's thin

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ### 3. Present and compare

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Present designs sequentially so the user can absorb each one, then compare them in prose. Contrast by **depth** (leverage at the interface), **locality** (where change concentrates), and **seam placement**.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: After comparing, give your own recommendation: which design you think is strongest and why. If elements from different designs would combine well, propose a hybrid. Be opinionated — the user wants a strong read, not a menu.
